doc.summary:
Capture tmux state in IO and process detached observations with ordinary
 Haskell collections. Start a private daemon with :obj:`withOwnedServer <LibTmux.Server#v:withOwnedServer>` or
 borrow one with :obj:`withServer <LibTmux.Server#v:withServer>`. Navigation and field access from
 :obj:`LibTmux.Snapshot <LibTmux.Snapshot>` perform no external operations.
 :obj:`renameSession <LibTmux.Server#v:renameSession>`, :obj:`renameWindow <LibTmux.Server#v:renameWindow>` and :obj:`setPaneTitle <LibTmux.Server#v:setPaneTitle>` act on explicit references
 in IO; detached observations change only when acquired again with :obj:`capture <LibTmux.Server#v:capture>`.
 :obj:`createSession <LibTmux.Server#v:createSession>`, :obj:`createWindow <LibTmux.Server#v:createWindow>` and :obj:`splitPane <LibTmux.Server#v:splitPane>` return historical identities;
 :obj:`LibTmux.Creation <LibTmux.Creation>` describes their options and explicit link context.
 :obj:`lookupPaneOccurrence <LibTmux.Snapshot#v:lookupPaneOccurrence>` resolves that context for :obj:`movePane <LibTmux.Server#v:movePane>`, :obj:`joinPane <LibTmux.Server#v:joinPane>`
 and :obj:`breakPane <LibTmux.Server#v:breakPane>`. Capture again to confirm the pane's placement.
 :obj:`resizePane <LibTmux.Server#v:resizePane>` and :obj:`resizeWindow <LibTmux.Server#v:resizeWindow>` request absolute cells through checked
 :obj:`Resize <LibTmux.Value#t:Resize>` values. Capture again for actual geometry.

Discover daemon-dependent application operations before creating resources.
 The table describes the complete Haskell operation, including its required
 exit observation. The general library admission floor remains separate.

Observe tmux control notifications from :obj:`withControl <LibTmux.Server#v:withControl>`.
 Read from the bounded queue in STM. The enclosing Server retains ownership

>>> fmap renderWindowId (parseWindowId "@17")
Right "@17"
>>> either (const "rejected") renderPaneId (parsePaneId "@17")

doc.body:
A scope sends TERM, waits up to 100ms for leader exit, then sends group KILL
 through a retained Linux pidfd.
 Completed cleanup proves leader exit and an empty retained process group.
 Zombies or uninterruptible members may leave a reachable cleanup recovery.
 Processes that move to another process group/session escape this contract.
 Linux 6.9 process-group pidfd signaling and a local daemon in the same PID
 and filesystem namespaces are required. The selected :obj:`bootstrapShell <LibTmux.Program#v:ProgramOptions.bootstrapShell>` must
 provide Bash dynamic descriptors, timed reads and execfail. It defaults to
 `/bin/bash` and is probed before application creation. The gate has a
 separate one-second startup lease; :obj:`commandTimeout <LibTmux.Program#v:ProgramOptions.commandTimeout>` bounds each native
 command. Neither bounds whole startup: :obj:`executionTimeout <LibTmux.Program#v:ProgramOptions.executionTimeout>` bounds owning
 setup and the callback. Cleanup wakes a blocked gate with an abort claim;
 the descriptor closes before application exec.
 The host operation and tmux 3.8 capability are checked before application
 resources are created.

Output is a bounded rendered snapshot, not stdout/stderr byte streaming.
 Controller-process crash recovery, persistent leases, readiness predicates,
 keep/detach and MCP operations remain unimplemented. Use the scope while its
 callback runs; detached :obj:`ProgramResult <LibTmux.Program#t:ProgramResult>` values survive cleanup.

 :obj:`runProgram <LibTmux.Server#v:runProgram>` for a final result. These operations borrow the
 selected daemon and own only their new session, application process group,
 native command clients, pin, buffers and files.

 an existing :obj:`Snapshot <LibTmux.Snapshot#t:Snapshot>` without IO. :obj:`fetch <LibTmux.Query#v:fetch>` explicitly acquires a new

Import :obj:`LibTmux.Query.Fields <LibTmux.Query.Fields>` qualified for row-prefixed tokens such as
 `F.paneActive` and `F.sessionWindowLinks`. They describe captured values;
 reading them never contacts tmux.

Query construction, operands and results are finite. Execution validates
 every declared requirement before filtering, stably ordering and limiting.
 The default source order and multiplicity come from the supplied snapshot.
 A result establishes what was observed, not current liveness or a reserved
 command target. See :obj:`exactlyOne <LibTmux.Query#v:exactlyOne>` before selecting an explicit reference.



```haskell
>>> exactlyOne [1 :: Integer]
Right 1
>>> exactlyOne ([] :: [Integer])
Left NoMatches
>>> atMostOne ([] :: [Integer])
Right Nothing
>>> atMostOne [1, 2 :: Integer]
Left AtLeastTwoMatches
```

A :obj:`Server <LibTmux.Server#t:Server>` represents one adoption of one endpoint. :obj:`withOwnedServer <LibTmux.Server#v:withOwnedServer>`
 starts and retires a private daemon. :obj:`withServer <LibTmux.Server#v:withServer>` borrows a daemon and
 releases its socket pin, native command clients and cleanup workers when
 the scope closes. The tmux noun `Client` refers to detached observations in
 :obj:`LibTmux.Snapshot <LibTmux.Snapshot>`.
 :obj:`withRuntime <LibTmux.Server#v:withRuntime>` and :obj:`withServerIn <LibTmux.Server#v:withServerIn>` give several handles shared resource limits
 and independent Server scopes.

:obj:`capture <LibTmux.Server#v:capture>` returns fully decoded, validated values. Field access and graph
 navigation are pure. Captures use an observation interval, not an atomic
 transaction over tmux and operating-system state.
 :obj:`createSession <LibTmux.Server#v:createSession>`, :obj:`createWindow <LibTmux.Server#v:createWindow>` and :obj:`splitPane <LibTmux.Server#v:splitPane>` return historical identities.
 :obj:`renameSession <LibTmux.Server#v:renameSession>`,
 :obj:`renameWindow <LibTmux.Server#v:renameWindow>` and :obj:`setPaneTitle <LibTmux.Server#v:setPaneTitle>` update generation-bound targets.
 :obj:`killServer <LibTmux.Server#v:killServer>`, :obj:`killSession <LibTmux.Server#v:killSession>`, :obj:`killWindow <LibTmux.Server#v:killWindow>` and :obj:`killPane <LibTmux.Server#v:killPane>` retire their targets.
 Capture again to observe their effects.

Operational failures use :obj:`TmuxException <LibTmux.Server#t:TmuxException>`. :obj:`tryTmux <LibTmux.Server#v:tryTmux>` catches that type only.
 Cancellation and callback failures keep their original exception class.
 Use :obj:`LibTmux.Recovery <LibTmux.Recovery>` to inspect retained owners after incomplete cleanup.

:obj:`LibTmux.Server <LibTmux.Server>` acquires a :obj:`Snapshot <LibTmux.Snapshot#t:Snapshot>` in IO. Every operation in this
 module reads owned Haskell values, including after the Server closes.
 Use ordinary lists, comprehensions and folds for application predicates.

:obj:`Window <LibTmux.Snapshot#t:Window>` and :obj:`Pane <LibTmux.Snapshot#t:Pane>` are physical entities. A :obj:`WindowLink <LibTmux.Snapshot#t:WindowLink>` identifies an
 observed session*index*window binding; :obj:`PaneOccurrence <LibTmux.Snapshot#t:PaneOccurrence>` retains that
 context. :obj:`paneOccurrences <LibTmux.Snapshot#v:paneOccurrences>` therefore preserves repeated appearances while
 :obj:`panes <LibTmux.Snapshot#v:panes>` lists each physical pane once.

References compare identity within one Server generation. A lookup reads
 the supplied snapshot, including a newer snapshot from that same Server.
 Independent Server scopes have different generations. Resolve an ID again
 with :obj:`lookupPaneId <LibTmux.Snapshot#v:lookupPaneId>` when deliberately selecting a newly observed entity.

Observation fields are exported for record dot and local updates. Editing
 a record does not change a snapshot's indexes or establish provenance.
 :obj:`LibTmux.Snapshot.Fixture <LibTmux.Snapshot.Fixture>` constructs validated offline snapshots;
 :obj:`snapshotOrigin <LibTmux.Snapshot#v:snapshotOrigin>` distinguishes them from observations acquired through IO.

 model successive observations; they never equal a live Server generation.
 Snapshot and live-reference constructors remain hidden.
 Validation checks graph and metadata laws; wire decoding, tmux normalization

Construction and access are pure. Window-link indices and pane indices
 have distinct types; neither substitutes for an entity ID. A constructor
 checks the mathematical domain, while command-specific limits belong at
 the operation boundary. Use :obj:`mkDimension <LibTmux.Value#v:mkDimension>`, :obj:`mkWindowIndex <LibTmux.Value#v:mkWindowIndex>` and :obj:`mkPaneIndex <LibTmux.Value#v:mkPaneIndex>`
 to validate input; their accessors return mathematical integers. Entity
 identifiers belong to :obj:`LibTmux.Id <LibTmux.Id>`.



```haskell
>>> fmap dimensionValue (mkDimension 120)
Right 120
>>> mkDimension 0
Left (NonPositiveDimension 0)
```

doc.body:
These functions consume supplied text. They neither execute `tmux -V`
 nor contact a server. Admission is a floor: every release at or above
 3.3a passes, with no upper bound. Admission says nothing about which
 releases the project has tested, and individual features still need
 capability and conformance checks.

Use :obj:`parseVersion <LibTmux.Version#v:parseVersion>` for input, :obj:`requireSupported <LibTmux.Version#v:requireSupported>` for minimum-version
 admission and :obj:`renderVersion <LibTmux.Version#v:renderVersion>` for the spelling tmux reports.



```haskell
>>> :set -XOverloadedStrings
>>> fmap renderVersion (parseVersion "tmux 3.3a\n" >>= requireSupported)
Right "3.3a"
```

Numeric components compare as numbers, and a patch letter follows its
 release:



```haskell
>>> (<) <$> parseVersion "3.9" <*> parseVersion "3.10"
Right True
>>> (<) <$> parseVersion "3.10" <*> parseVersion "3.10a"
Right True
```

A development build or release candidate ranks below the release it
 precedes:



```haskell
>>> (<) <$> parseVersion "next-3.10" <*> parseVersion "3.10-rc"
Right True
>>> (<) <$> parseVersion "3.10-rc2" <*> parseVersion "3.10"
Right True
```

### What is on here

Calls that find, read or change a session, by job. The calls that take a
 `Server` contact tmux; the rest read values you already hold.

**Get the sessions in a snapshot.** Capture a snapshot through a Server,
 then list its sessions in ID order or start a query from them.


- From a Server: :obj:`capture <LibTmux.Server#v:capture>`
- From a snapshot: :obj:`sessions <LibTmux.Snapshot#v:sessions>`
- As a query source: :obj:`sessions <LibTmux.Query#v:sessions>`

**Find a session by reference or ID.** A lookup reads the snapshot you pass
 and returns a lookup error for a missing or foreign reference. An ID selects
 whichever session holds it in that snapshot, with no continuity with an
 earlier Server.

:obj:`lookupSession <LibTmux.Snapshot#v:lookupSession>`, :obj:`lookupSessionId <LibTmux.Snapshot#v:lookupSessionId>`,
 :obj:`SessionRef <LibTmux.Snapshot#t:SessionRef>`, :obj:`LookupError <LibTmux.Snapshot#t:LookupError>`

**Parse and print session IDs.** Parsing and rendering are pure. An ID
 carries no endpoint or liveness evidence.

:obj:`parseSessionId <LibTmux.Id#v:parseSessionId>`, :obj:`renderSessionId <LibTmux.Id#v:renderSessionId>`,
 :obj:`sessionIdValue <LibTmux.Id#v:sessionIdValue>`, :obj:`sessionId <LibTmux.Snapshot#v:sessionId>`, :obj:`SessionId <LibTmux.Id#t:SessionId>`

**Read a session's fields.** Use record dot on the value, or a field token
 in a query. Field tokens describe captured values and never contact tmux.

:obj:`sessionId <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:sessionId>`, :obj:`sessionName <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:sessionName>`,
 :obj:`sessionAttached <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:sessionAttached>`, :obj:`sessionGroup <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:sessionGroup>`

**Follow a session to its windows and clients, or back.** A session reaches
 its windows through links, and one window can be linked more than once. A
 window link and a client attachment each name a session; resolve it in a
 query.


- From a snapshot: :obj:`linksForSession <LibTmux.Snapshot#v:linksForSession>`
- From a session in a query: :obj:`sessionWindowLinks <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:sessionWindowLinks>`,
   :obj:`sessionClients <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:sessionClients>`
- Test its links or clients: :obj:`some <LibTmux.Query#v:some>`, :obj:`every <LibTmux.Query#v:every>`,
   :obj:`none <LibTmux.Query#v:none>`
- From a window link: :obj:`linkSessionId <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:linkSessionId>`,
   :obj:`linkSession <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:linkSession>`
- From a client attachment: :obj:`clientAttachmentSessionId <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:clientAttachmentSessionId>`,
   :obj:`clientAttachmentSession <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:clientAttachmentSession>`
- Resolve the session: :obj:`related <LibTmux.Query#v:related>`

**Select sessions with a query.** Match the name by equality or an exact
 substring and the attached count by a threshold, then run the query on a
 snapshot you hold or fetch a fresh one. `exactlyOne` turns a result into one
 session or an error.

:obj:`sessions <LibTmux.Query#v:sessions>`, :obj:`matching <LibTmux.Query#v:matching>`, :obj:`eq <LibTmux.Query#v:eq>`,
 :obj:`contains <LibTmux.Query#v:contains>`, :obj:`ge <LibTmux.Query#v:ge>`, :obj:`runQuery <LibTmux.Query#v:runQuery>`,
 :obj:`fetch <LibTmux.Query#v:fetch>`, :obj:`exactlyOne <LibTmux.Query#v:exactlyOne>`

**Create a session.** Creation returns the references tmux printed, not an
 observed session. Capture again to see the new session. A failed creation
 can leave a receipt in its recovery, and a missing receipt does not mean no
 session exists.


- Create: :obj:`createSession <LibTmux.Server#v:createSession>`, :obj:`createSessionWith <LibTmux.Server#v:createSessionWith>`
- Describe: :obj:`defaultSessionOptions <LibTmux.Creation#v:defaultSessionOptions>`,
   :obj:`SessionOptions <LibTmux.Creation#t:SessionOptions>`, :obj:`CreatedSession <LibTmux.Creation#t:CreatedSession>`
- After a failure: :obj:`creationReceipt <LibTmux.Recovery#v:creationReceipt>`

**Rename a session.** The name is literal text, and snapshots you already
 hold keep the old name. A reference from another Server or an offline
 fixture is refused before the command runs. The `With` variant takes a
 deadline.

:obj:`renameSession <LibTmux.Server#v:renameSession>`, :obj:`renameSessionWith <LibTmux.Server#v:renameSessionWith>`

**Read or change session settings.** Use the captured session reference
 to select an option or environment store. Read a local option for the
 override, or read an effective option to include inheritance.


- Use :obj:`SessionOptionsAt <LibTmux.Options#v:SessionOptionsAt>` with :obj:`readOption <LibTmux.Server#v:readOption>`
   or :obj:`setOption <LibTmux.Server#v:setOption>`.
- Use :obj:`SessionEnvironment <LibTmux.Environment#v:SessionEnvironment>` with
   :obj:`getEnvironment <LibTmux.Server#v:getEnvironment>` or :obj:`setEnvironment <LibTmux.Server#v:setEnvironment>`.
- [Session settings example](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-haskell/blob/1257155c45f95f620a546f0f45671ef4558cd122/docs/options.md#select-a-store)

**Add a window to a session.** A placement names the session and where the
 window goes: the next free index or a slot. The result holds the references
 tmux printed, so capture again to observe the window.


- Create: :obj:`createWindow <LibTmux.Server#v:createWindow>`, :obj:`createWindowWith <LibTmux.Server#v:createWindowWith>`
- Place: :obj:`WindowPlacement <LibTmux.Creation#t:WindowPlacement>`, :obj:`WindowSlot <LibTmux.Creation#t:WindowSlot>`

:obj:`killSession <LibTmux.Server#v:killSession>`, :obj:`killSessionWith <LibTmux.Server#v:killSessionWith>`

**Change which windows a session links.** A slot names the session and the

- Select: :obj:`selectWindowLink <LibTmux.Server#v:selectWindowLink>`,

- Link: :obj:`linkWindow <LibTmux.Server#v:linkWindow>`, :obj:`linkWindowWith <LibTmux.Server#v:linkWindowWith>`
- Unlink: :obj:`unlinkWindow <LibTmux.Server#v:unlinkWindow>`, :obj:`unlinkWindowWith <LibTmux.Server#v:unlinkWindowWith>`

 :obj:`windowIdValue <LibTmux.Id#v:windowIdValue>`, :obj:`windowId <LibTmux.Snapshot#v:windowId>`, :obj:`WindowId <LibTmux.Id#t:WindowId>`

**Read a window's fields.** Use record dot on the value, or a field token in
 a query. The name keeps the bytes tmux reports, because older supported
 releases can retain names that are not valid UTF-8; decode it as UTF-8 when
 you need text.


- Field tokens: :obj:`windowId <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:windowId>`, :obj:`windowName <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:windowName>`,
   :obj:`windowWidth <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:windowWidth>`, :obj:`windowHeight <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:windowHeight>`,
   :obj:`windowLayout <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:windowLayout>`, :obj:`windowZoomed <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:windowZoomed>`
- The name as bytes: :obj:`TmuxText <LibTmux.Snapshot#t:TmuxText>`, :obj:`labelText <LibTmux.Snapshot#v:labelText>`,
   :obj:`labelBytes <LibTmux.Snapshot#v:labelBytes>`, :obj:`labelFromBytes <LibTmux.Snapshot#v:labelFromBytes>`

**Follow a window to its panes and links.** Panes come in pane-index order.
 One window can have several links, and its name and pane set are shared
 across them.


- From a snapshot: :obj:`panesForWindow <LibTmux.Snapshot#v:panesForWindow>`
- From a window in a query: :obj:`windowPanes <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:windowPanes>`,
   :obj:`windowLinks <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:windowLinks>`
- Test its panes or links: :obj:`some <LibTmux.Query#v:some>`, :obj:`every <LibTmux.Query#v:every>`,
   :obj:`none <LibTmux.Query#v:none>`
- From a window link: :obj:`linkPanes <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:linkPanes>`

**Reach a window from a link, a pane or a client.** Each names one window;
 resolve it in a query.


- From a window link: :obj:`linkWindowId <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:linkWindowId>`,
   :obj:`linkWindow <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:linkWindow>`
- From a pane: :obj:`paneWindowId <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:paneWindowId>`, :obj:`paneWindow <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:paneWindow>`
- From a client attachment: :obj:`clientAttachmentWindowId <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:clientAttachmentWindowId>`,
   :obj:`clientAttachmentWindow <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:clientAttachmentWindow>`
- Resolve the window: :obj:`related <LibTmux.Query#v:related>`

**Read where a window sits in a session.** A window's index belongs to a
 link in one session, not to the window, and reindexing can change it.


- Index type: :obj:`WindowIndex <LibTmux.Value#t:WindowIndex>`, :obj:`mkWindowIndex <LibTmux.Value#v:mkWindowIndex>`,
   :obj:`windowIndexValue <LibTmux.Value#v:windowIndexValue>`
- Field tokens: :obj:`linkIndex <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:linkIndex>`,
   :obj:`clientAttachmentWindowIndex <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:clientAttachmentWindowIndex>`
- Thresholds: :obj:`windowIndexAtLeast <LibTmux.Query#v:windowIndexAtLeast>`,
   :obj:`windowIndexAtMost <LibTmux.Query#v:windowIndexAtMost>`

**Select windows with a query.** Compare sizes with a dimension threshold.
 Names are bytes, so match them with exact equality rather than a substring.

:obj:`windows <LibTmux.Query#v:windows>`, :obj:`matching <LibTmux.Query#v:matching>`, :obj:`eq <LibTmux.Query#v:eq>`,
 :obj:`dimensionAtLeast <LibTmux.Query#v:dimensionAtLeast>`, :obj:`dimensionAtMost <LibTmux.Query#v:dimensionAtMost>`,
 :obj:`runQuery <LibTmux.Query#v:runQuery>`, :obj:`fetch <LibTmux.Query#v:fetch>`

**Create a window.** A placement says where it goes, and the options set a
 label, a directory, an environment, whether to select it and what to do with
 an occupied slot, which is refused by default. The result holds the
 references tmux printed, so capture again to observe the window.


- Create: :obj:`createWindow <LibTmux.Server#v:createWindow>`, :obj:`createWindowWith <LibTmux.Server#v:createWindowWith>`
- Place: :obj:`WindowPlacement <LibTmux.Creation#t:WindowPlacement>`, :obj:`WindowSlot <LibTmux.Creation#t:WindowSlot>`,
   :obj:`WindowCollision <LibTmux.Creation#t:WindowCollision>`
- Options: :obj:`WindowOptions <LibTmux.Creation#t:WindowOptions>`,
   :obj:`defaultWindowOptions <LibTmux.Creation#v:defaultWindowOptions>`
- Result: :obj:`CreatedWindow <LibTmux.Creation#t:CreatedWindow>`

**Get the window a new session starts with.** Creating a session returns
 the reference and link index of its first window. Capture again to observe
 the window.

:obj:`createSession <LibTmux.Server#v:createSession>`, :obj:`createSessionWith <LibTmux.Server#v:createSessionWith>`,
 :obj:`CreatedSession <LibTmux.Creation#t:CreatedSession>`

**Rename a window.** One rename changes the physical window across all its
 session links. The label keeps its bytes, and tmux may reject names its
 release does not accept. A reference from another Server or an offline
 fixture is refused before the command runs.

:obj:`renameWindow <LibTmux.Server#v:renameWindow>`, :obj:`renameWindowWith <LibTmux.Server#v:renameWindowWith>`

**Link a window into another slot, or remove a link.** A slot names a session
 and a link index. Linking puts the window in a vacant slot; existing links
 remain and the new link starts unselected. tmux refuses to remove a window's
 last link, and session groups can propagate either change.


- Link: :obj:`linkWindow <LibTmux.Server#v:linkWindow>`, :obj:`linkWindowWith <LibTmux.Server#v:linkWindowWith>`
- Unlink: :obj:`unlinkWindow <LibTmux.Server#v:unlinkWindow>`, :obj:`unlinkWindowWith <LibTmux.Server#v:unlinkWindowWith>`
- Slot: :obj:`WindowSlot <LibTmux.Creation#t:WindowSlot>`

**Select a window link.** Selection works on a link, so it can pick one of
 several links to the same physical window. Capture again to observe it.

:obj:`selectWindowLink <LibTmux.Server#v:selectWindowLink>`, :obj:`selectWindowLinkWith <LibTmux.Server#v:selectWindowLinkWith>`,
 :obj:`WindowSlot <LibTmux.Creation#t:WindowSlot>`

**Arrange a window's panes with a named layout.** Every link to the window
 sees the new layout, and tmux can unzoom the window. Capture again to observe
 the pane geometry.

:obj:`selectLayout <LibTmux.Server#v:selectLayout>`, :obj:`selectLayoutWith <LibTmux.Server#v:selectLayoutWith>`,
 :obj:`NamedLayout <LibTmux.Server#t:NamedLayout>`

**Resize a window.** Request an absolute width, height or both with
 :obj:`Resize <LibTmux.Value#t:Resize>` and dimensions from :obj:`mkDimension <LibTmux.Value#v:mkDimension>`.
 Capture again for the size tmux applied.

:obj:`resizeWindow <LibTmux.Server#v:resizeWindow>`, :obj:`resizeWindowWith <LibTmux.Server#v:resizeWindowWith>`,
 [Resize example](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-haskell/blob/1257155c45f95f620a546f0f45671ef4558cd122/docs/resizing.md)

**Remove a window.** One removal closes the physical window across all its
 links, and tmux closes a session left without windows.

:obj:`killWindow <LibTmux.Server#v:killWindow>`, :obj:`killWindowWith <LibTmux.Server#v:killWindowWith>`

**Build a window offline.** Fixture references belong to a named offline
 origin, never to a live Server. Validation checks a fixture before it
 becomes a snapshot.

:obj:`windowRef <LibTmux.Snapshot.Fixture#v:windowRef>`,
 :obj:`validateFixture <LibTmux.Snapshot.Fixture#v:validateFixture>`,
 :obj:`Fixture <LibTmux.Snapshot.Fixture#t:Fixture>`

doc.body:
### What is on here

Calls that find, read or change a pane, by job. The calls that take a
 `Server` contact tmux; the rest read values you already hold.

**Get the panes in a snapshot.** The pane lists show each physical pane
 once; the occurrence lists keep every appearance, including repeats through
 several links.


- From a Server: :obj:`capture <LibTmux.Server#v:capture>`
- From a snapshot: :obj:`panes <LibTmux.Snapshot#v:panes>`,
   :obj:`paneOccurrences <LibTmux.Snapshot#v:paneOccurrences>`
- As a query source: :obj:`panes <LibTmux.Query#v:panes>`, :obj:`paneOccurrences <LibTmux.Query#v:paneOccurrences>`

**Find a pane by reference or ID.** A lookup reads the snapshot you pass and
 returns a lookup error for a missing or foreign reference. An ID selects
 whichever pane holds it in that snapshot.

:obj:`lookupPane <LibTmux.Snapshot#v:lookupPane>`, :obj:`lookupPaneId <LibTmux.Snapshot#v:lookupPaneId>`, :obj:`PaneRef <LibTmux.Snapshot#t:PaneRef>`,
 :obj:`LookupError <LibTmux.Snapshot#t:LookupError>`

**Parse and print pane IDs.** Parsing and rendering are pure. An ID carries
 no endpoint or liveness evidence.

:obj:`parsePaneId <LibTmux.Id#v:parsePaneId>`, :obj:`renderPaneId <LibTmux.Id#v:renderPaneId>`,
 :obj:`paneIdValue <LibTmux.Id#v:paneIdValue>`, :obj:`paneId <LibTmux.Snapshot#v:paneId>`, :obj:`PaneId <LibTmux.Id#t:PaneId>`

**Read a pane's fields.** Use record dot on the value, or a field token in a
 query. The title is UTF-8 text; the command and path keep the POSIX bytes
 from the endpoint.

:obj:`paneId <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:paneId>`, :obj:`paneWindowId <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:paneWindowId>`,
 :obj:`paneIndex <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:paneIndex>`, :obj:`paneWidth <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:paneWidth>`,
 :obj:`paneHeight <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:paneHeight>`, :obj:`paneActive <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:paneActive>`,
 :obj:`paneDead <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:paneDead>`, :obj:`paneTitle <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:paneTitle>`,
 :obj:`paneCurrentCommand <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:paneCurrentCommand>`, :obj:`paneCurrentPath <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:paneCurrentPath>`,
 :obj:`paneCursorX <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:paneCursorX>`, :obj:`paneCursorY <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:paneCursorY>`,
 :obj:`paneModeCount <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:paneModeCount>`, :obj:`paneMode <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:paneMode>`

**Follow a pane to its window and back.** A window's panes come in
 pane-index order. Resolve a pane's window in a query.


- From a pane in a query: :obj:`paneWindow <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:paneWindow>`
- Resolve the window: :obj:`related <LibTmux.Query#v:related>`
- From a snapshot: :obj:`panesForWindow <LibTmux.Snapshot#v:panesForWindow>`
- From a window in a query: :obj:`windowPanes <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:windowPanes>`
- From a window link: :obj:`linkPanes <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:linkPanes>`
- Test a window's panes: :obj:`some <LibTmux.Query#v:some>`, :obj:`every <LibTmux.Query#v:every>`,
   :obj:`none <LibTmux.Query#v:none>`

**Keep the context a pane appears in.** An occurrence pairs a physical pane
 with one window link, and a client attachment selects a pane in its actual
 session and index.


- From a pane occurrence: :obj:`occurrencePane <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:occurrencePane>`,
   :obj:`occurrenceLink <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:occurrenceLink>`
- From a client attachment: :obj:`clientAttachmentPaneId <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:clientAttachmentPaneId>`,
   :obj:`clientAttachmentPane <LibTmux.Query.Fields#v:clientAttachmentPane>`
- Occurrence type: :obj:`PaneOccurrence <LibTmux.Snapshot#t:PaneOccurrence>`

**Select panes with a query.** Compare sizes and indices with thresholds,
 and match the title by equality or an exact substring.

:obj:`panes <LibTmux.Query#v:panes>`, :obj:`matching <LibTmux.Query#v:matching>`, :obj:`eq <LibTmux.Query#v:eq>`,
 :obj:`contains <LibTmux.Query#v:contains>`, :obj:`dimensionAtLeast <LibTmux.Query#v:dimensionAtLeast>`,
 :obj:`dimensionAtMost <LibTmux.Query#v:dimensionAtMost>`, :obj:`paneIndexAtLeast <LibTmux.Query#v:paneIndexAtLeast>`,
 :obj:`paneIndexAtMost <LibTmux.Query#v:paneIndexAtMost>`, :obj:`runQuery <LibTmux.Query#v:runQuery>`,
 :obj:`fetch <LibTmux.Query#v:fetch>`

**Validate a pane index or size.** Construction checks the mathematical
 domain, and the accessors return integers.


- Pane index: :obj:`PaneIndex <LibTmux.Value#t:PaneIndex>`, :obj:`mkPaneIndex <LibTmux.Value#v:mkPaneIndex>`,
   :obj:`paneIndexValue <LibTmux.Value#v:paneIndexValue>`
- Size: :obj:`Dimension <LibTmux.Value#t:Dimension>`, :obj:`mkDimension <LibTmux.Value#v:mkDimension>`,
   :obj:`dimensionValue <LibTmux.Value#v:dimensionValue>`

**Get the first pane of a new session or window.** Creating one returns the
 reference of its first pane. Capture again to observe the pane.

:obj:`createSession <LibTmux.Server#v:createSession>`, :obj:`createSessionWith <LibTmux.Server#v:createSessionWith>`,
 :obj:`createWindow <LibTmux.Server#v:createWindow>`, :obj:`createWindowWith <LibTmux.Server#v:createWindowWith>`,
 :obj:`CreatedEntities <LibTmux.Creation#t:CreatedEntities>`

**Split a pane.** Name the pane and the session slot that holds its window,
 then choose a direction and a size. The slot must hold that pane's window
 when tmux runs the command, and the size is a request that tmux can clamp or
 refuse. The result records the new pane and the context it was split in.


- Split: :obj:`splitPane <LibTmux.Server#v:splitPane>`, :obj:`splitPaneWith <LibTmux.Server#v:splitPaneWith>`
- Options: :obj:`SplitOptions <LibTmux.Creation#t:SplitOptions>`,
   :obj:`defaultSplitOptions <LibTmux.Creation#v:defaultSplitOptions>`, :obj:`SplitDirection <LibTmux.Creation#t:SplitDirection>`,
   :obj:`SplitSize <LibTmux.Creation#t:SplitSize>`
- Slot and result: :obj:`WindowSlot <LibTmux.Creation#t:WindowSlot>`,
   :obj:`CreatedPane <LibTmux.Creation#t:CreatedPane>`

**Select a pane.** Name the pane and the window link that holds it. tmux
 rejects a pane that no longer belongs to that link's current window.

:obj:`selectExactPane <LibTmux.Server#v:selectExactPane>`, :obj:`selectExactPaneWith <LibTmux.Server#v:selectExactPaneWith>`,
 :obj:`WindowSlot <LibTmux.Creation#t:WindowSlot>`

**Arrange the panes of a window.** A named layout applies to the physical
 window at a slot and changes the geometry of its panes. Capture again to
 observe the result.

:obj:`selectLayout <LibTmux.Server#v:selectLayout>`, :obj:`selectLayoutWith <LibTmux.Server#v:selectLayoutWith>`,
 :obj:`NamedLayout <LibTmux.Server#t:NamedLayout>`, :obj:`WindowSlot <LibTmux.Creation#t:WindowSlot>`

**Set a pane's title.** The title is literal text, and the pane's
 application can replace it later. A reference from another Server or an
 offline fixture is refused before the command runs.

:obj:`setPaneTitle <LibTmux.Server#v:setPaneTitle>`, :obj:`setPaneTitleWith <LibTmux.Server#v:setPaneTitleWith>`

**Resize a pane.** Request an absolute width, height or both for its
 reference. The native layout can resize neighboring panes.

:obj:`resizePane <LibTmux.Server#v:resizePane>`, :obj:`resizePaneWith <LibTmux.Server#v:resizePaneWith>`,
 :obj:`mkDimension <LibTmux.Value#v:mkDimension>`,
 [Resize example](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-haskell/blob/1257155c45f95f620a546f0f45671ef4558cd122/docs/resizing.md)

**Move a running pane.** Resolve its exact session link with
 :obj:`lookupPaneOccurrence <LibTmux.Snapshot#v:lookupPaneOccurrence>`. Capture the new slot after
 :obj:`movePane <LibTmux.Server#v:movePane>`, :obj:`joinPane <LibTmux.Server#v:joinPane>` or
 :obj:`breakPane <LibTmux.Server#v:breakPane>`.

**Send input to a pane.** Send literal text, or named tmux keys such as
 `Enter` in order. Nothing appends Enter, and success confirms that tmux
 processed the request, not that the application responded. An invalid key
 name raises an error before any key is typed.

:obj:`sendKeys <LibTmux.Server#v:sendKeys>`, :obj:`sendKeysWith <LibTmux.Server#v:sendKeysWith>`,
 :obj:`PaneInput <LibTmux.Server#t:PaneInput>`

**Paste a named buffer.** Pass the buffer name, an exact pane reference
 and a :obj:`PasteNewlines <LibTmux.Pane#t:PasteNewlines>` policy.

:obj:`pasteBuffer <LibTmux.Server#v:pasteBuffer>`, :obj:`loadBuffer <LibTmux.Server#v:loadBuffer>`,
 [Paste example](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-haskell/blob/1257155c45f95f620a546f0f45671ef4558cd122/docs/buffers.md)

**Read a pane's text.** Capture the visible rows or a range, as plain text or
 with ANSI styling, within a byte limit. The result is a detached observation,
 and reading its text contacts no daemon.


- Capture: :obj:`capturePane <LibTmux.Server#v:capturePane>`
- Options: :obj:`PaneCaptureOptions <LibTmux.Pane#t:PaneCaptureOptions>`,
   :obj:`defaultPaneCapture <LibTmux.Pane#v:defaultPaneCapture>`, :obj:`PaneRows <LibTmux.Pane#t:PaneRows>`,
   :obj:`PaneRendering <LibTmux.Pane#t:PaneRendering>`
- Read: :obj:`PaneText <LibTmux.Server#t:PaneText>`, :obj:`paneText <LibTmux.Server#v:paneText>`

**Wait for text in a pane.** Poll one exact pane for a case-sensitive
 substring under a single deadline of at most ten seconds. Presence can match
 text already on screen; a fresh match compares with a capture taken before
 the input and ignores that text. A timeout or the pane's exit still returns
 the last capture when one completed.

:obj:`waitForText <LibTmux.Server#v:waitForText>`, :obj:`PaneWaitOptions <LibTmux.Server#t:PaneWaitOptions>`,
 :obj:`defaultPaneWait <LibTmux.Server#v:defaultPaneWait>`, :obj:`PaneMatch <LibTmux.Server#t:PaneMatch>`,
 :obj:`PaneWaitResult <LibTmux.Server#t:PaneWaitResult>`

**Wait for a pane state.** Wait for retained death, disappearance or focus
 through a session link. A match carries the snapshot that confirmed it.

:obj:`waitForPaneState <LibTmux.Server#v:waitForPaneState>`, :obj:`PaneState <LibTmux.Server#t:PaneState>`,
 :obj:`PaneStateWaitResult <LibTmux.Server#t:PaneStateWaitResult>`

**Remove a pane.** Removing the last pane also closes its window. Success
 confirms that tmux removed the pane, so observe its processes' exit
 separately.

:obj:`killPane <LibTmux.Server#v:killPane>`, :obj:`killPaneWith <LibTmux.Server#v:killPaneWith>`

**Build a pane offline.** Fixture references belong to a named offline
 origin, never to a live Server. Validation checks a fixture before it
 becomes a snapshot.

:obj:`paneRef <LibTmux.Snapshot.Fixture#v:paneRef>`,
 :obj:`validateFixture <LibTmux.Snapshot.Fixture#v:validateFixture>`,
 :obj:`Fixture <LibTmux.Snapshot.Fixture#t:Fixture>`

Parse a release identity or the output of `tmux -V`, allowing a leading
 `tmux ` and one final LF. The accepted forms are `X.Y`, `X.Ya`, `X.Y-rc`,
 `X.Y-rcN` and `next-X.Y`. Unknown suffixes, including a bare `master`, are
 rejected rather than assigned a guessed release. Diagnostics retain at most
 64 chars.
